# Workflows and presets

## Prerequisites

- The Data and Search Platform is deployed: `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}`
- You can reach it with one of: `curl`, the Sherlock Python SDK (`sherlock-client`), or the platform CLI ([`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli)).
- You have created a search store — see [Creating search stores](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/creating-search-stores.html).

## Client setup

Each example below is shown for three clients. All three call the same REST API at `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}/api/v1`; the SDK and the CLI wrap the requests shown in the **curl** tab. Every request requires a bearer token. The deployment’s IAM sidecar validates the token and adds the caller’s user identity to the request, and Sherlock authorizes the request against that identity.

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

Log in once with the platform CLI, then export the deployment URL and a token:

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser

export SHERLOCK_URL="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}"
export AA_TOKEN="$(pharia --env aleph-alpha iam token)"
```

Pass `-H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"` on every call. A platform token from any other source also works; the API only reads the header. Requests with a JSON body use `--json` (curl 7.82.0 or later), which sends the body and sets the `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers to `application/json`. To read the body from a file, use `--json @body.json`.

Install the client from the Aleph Alpha package index:

```bash
pip install sherlock-client --extra-index-url https://alephalpha.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/pypi/holmes/simple
```

Then create a client for the deployment and a handle for the store whose workflows you are configuring:

```python
import os

from sherlock import SyncSherlock

client = SyncSherlock(
    url="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}",
    token=os.environ["AA_TOKEN"],
)

store = client.v1.search_stores("<store-id>")
```

`url` and `token` default to the `SHERLOCK_BASE_URL` and `SHERLOCK_TOKEN` environment variables, so `SyncSherlock()` without arguments works when those variables are set. `Sherlock` is the async client and has the same API. Use either client as a context manager (`with SyncSherlock(...) as client:`) to close the connection pool when you finish.

The platform CLI ([`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli)) handles authentication. Log in once; every subsequent command uses the cached token:

```bash
pharia iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser
```

Select the environment with the global `--env` flag, for example `pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login`. The CLI caches tokens per environment and refreshes them automatically. To reach a deployment that the CLI does not know, pass `--base-url https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}` or set `PHARIA_SHERLOCK_URL`. To use the token in your own tooling, print it with `TOKEN=$(pharia iam token)`.

![Overview of the pharia iam commands](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/COMMON/_images/pharia-data-cli-iam.png)

## Built-in presets

Every ingestion workflow is based on a preset that defines defaults for extraction, chunking, and embedding. Select a preset when you create a workflow:

| Preset | Description |
|---|---|
| `DocumentAI` | Full pipeline: extraction, chunking, and embeddings. Use it for most use cases. |
| `DocumentAIFull` | `DocumentAI`, plus page-level enrichment such as keyword extraction. |

## Configuring a workflow

Create a workflow on your search store. Specify a preset and the parameters to use. Parameters are grouped by pipeline module: one group per reader, plus `chunker` and `vectorize`. The create call currently also requires the run-input `schema`:

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

`parameters` and `schema` are plain objects in the request body. This example uses the text-extraction document from Text extraction below:

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "name": "text-ingestion",
    "workflow_name": "DocumentAI",
    "parameters": {
      "chunker": {
        "batch_size": 1000,
        "chunk_overlap": 600,
        "chunk_size": 4096,
        "include_image_descriptions": false,
        "kind": "recursive"
      },
      "docx_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "doc",
        "split_level": 1
      },
      "markdown_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "markdown"
      },
      "pdf_reader": {
        "batch_size": 10,
        "kind": "pdf_text",
        "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"
      },
      "plaintext_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "plaintext",
        "max_content_size": 500000,
        "min_space_ratio": 0.02
      },
      "pptx_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "include_notes": true,
        "kind": "pptx"
      },
      "vectorize": {
        "batch_size": 10,
        "distance": "cosine",
        "kind": "openai_vectorize",
        "modality": "text",
        "provider": "pharia",
        "vector_type": "dense"
      },
      "xlsx_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "excel",
        "split_level": 2
      }
    },
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "source": {
          "description": "Source path, connector URI, or list thereof",
          "anyOf": [
            {"type": "string"},
            {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
          ]
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": true
    }
  }'
```

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

workflow = store.workflows.create(
    name="text-ingestion",
    workflow_name="DocumentAI",
    parameters=json.loads(Path("parameters.json").read_text()),
    schema=json.loads(Path("input-schema.json").read_text()),
)

print(workflow.id)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock workflows create <store-id> \
  --name text-ingestion \
  --workflow-name DocumentAI \
  --parameters @parameters.json \
  --schema @input-schema.json
```

The `schema` property (the run-input schema) is currently required but planned for deprecation.

The following sections contain two complete `parameters` documents that you can use without changes. Always send the whole document. Updates replace the entire object and do not merge it, so `workflows update` takes the same shape.

### Text extraction

`pdf_reader.kind: "pdf_text"` extracts the text layer directly from the PDF. It is fast, low-cost, and the recommended default for digitally created documents. This configuration uses no vision model, so the document has no `vision_reader` group:

```json
{
  "chunker": {
    "batch_size": 1000,
    "chunk_overlap": 600,
    "chunk_size": 4096,
    "include_image_descriptions": false,
    "kind": "recursive"
  },
  "docx_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "doc",
    "split_level": 1
  },
  "markdown_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "markdown"
  },
  "pdf_reader": {
    "batch_size": 10,
    "kind": "pdf_text",
    "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"
  },
  "plaintext_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "plaintext",
    "max_content_size": 500000,
    "min_space_ratio": 0.02
  },
  "pptx_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "include_notes": true,
    "kind": "pptx"
  },
  "vectorize": {
    "batch_size": 10,
    "distance": "cosine",
    "kind": "openai_vectorize",
    "modality": "text",
    "provider": "pharia",
    "vector_type": "dense"
  },
  "xlsx_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "excel",
    "split_level": 2
  }
}
```

Like `pdf_reader`, `docx_reader` and `xlsx_reader` select their implementation with `kind`. The default kinds are `doc` and `excel`, which use anydoc. They parse the file into markdown content blocks and start a new page at each heading. `split_level` sets the heading level that starts a new page. For documents without headings, `max_page_chars` (default 10000) limits the page size. Each Excel sheet surfaces as a level-2 heading, so the default `split_level: 2` gives one page per sheet. The previous implementations stay available as `"kind": "docx"` (python-docx) and `"kind": "xlsx"` (openpyxl).

| | Version availability The `doc` kind is available from release 0.8.10. The `excel` kind follows in the next release. Older deployments accept only the `docx` and `xlsx` kinds. |
|---|---|

With this configuration, scanned pages and pages whose content is in diagrams produce empty or garbled text. Use the vision configuration for these documents. For documents that mix digital and scanned pages, set `pdf_reader.kind` to `smart_pdf_router` instead. It extracts the text of each page that has a usable text layer and sends only the other pages to the vision model. It also requires a `vision_reader` group. See [Recipe: per-page routing](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/configuring-workflows.html#recipe-per-page-routing).

### Vision and OCR

Set `pdf_reader.kind` to `pdf_rasterizer` to render every page to an image instead of reading its text layer. This requires a `vision_reader` group, which converts the images to text. The rest of the document does not change:

```json
{
  "chunker": {
    "batch_size": 1000,
    "chunk_overlap": 600,
    "chunk_size": 4096,
    "include_image_descriptions": false,
    "kind": "recursive"
  },
  "docx_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "doc",
    "split_level": 1
  },
  "markdown_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "markdown"
  },
  "pdf_reader": {
    "batch_size": 10,
    "kind": "pdf_rasterizer",
    "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"
  },
  "plaintext_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "plaintext",
    "max_content_size": 500000,
    "min_space_ratio": 0.02
  },
  "pptx_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "include_notes": true,
    "kind": "pptx"
  },
  "vectorize": {
    "batch_size": 10,
    "distance": "cosine",
    "kind": "openai_vectorize",
    "modality": "text",
    "provider": "pharia",
    "vector_type": "dense"
  },
  "vision_reader": {
    "batch_size": 1,
    "extra_body": {
      "chat_template_kwargs": {
        "thinking": false
      }
    },
    "max_in_flight": 16,
    "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr",
    "provider": "d_inference",
    "temperature": 0,
    "timeout": 120
  },
  "xlsx_reader": {
    "batch_size": 100,
    "kind": "excel",
    "split_level": 2
  }
}
```

`vision_reader` does not need a `kind`, because only one module implements it; its `kind` defaults to `vision`. For `pdf_reader`, the `kind` field selects `pdf_text`, `pdf_rasterizer`, `smart_pdf_router`, or `pdf_router`. `vision_reader` requires `provider` and `model`; there is no default endpoint. They identify an inference deployment, not an embedding deployment. In this example, it is a vision-OCR model served through `d_inference`.

`extra_body` is sent to the model unchanged on every call; this example disables the model’s thinking mode. `temperature: 0` makes sampling deterministic, so the same page always produces the same text. Use this setting for OCR. If you do not set it, the model server’s default applies (Holmes builds before 0.8.7 ignore the field). `batch_size: 1` with `max_in_flight: 16` sends one page per call, with up to sixteen concurrent calls. Use this configuration when each unit of work is a model request rather than local computation.

This configuration is slower and more expensive per page than `pdf_text`. Set the `timeout` for the slowest page you need to process, not for the average page.

Run the new workflow the same way as the default workflow. See [Ingesting files](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/ingesting-files.html).

## Updating parameters

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

Send the whole `parameters` document, not only the groups you changed. This body switches the workflow created above to the vision configuration: `pdf_reader.kind` is `pdf_rasterizer` and a `vision_reader` group is added:

```bash
curl -X PUT "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows/<workflow-id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "parameters": {
      "chunker": {
        "batch_size": 1000,
        "chunk_overlap": 600,
        "chunk_size": 4096,
        "include_image_descriptions": false,
        "kind": "recursive"
      },
      "docx_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "doc",
        "split_level": 1
      },
      "markdown_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "markdown"
      },
      "pdf_reader": {
        "batch_size": 10,
        "kind": "pdf_rasterizer",
        "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"
      },
      "plaintext_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "plaintext",
        "max_content_size": 500000,
        "min_space_ratio": 0.02
      },
      "pptx_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "include_notes": true,
        "kind": "pptx"
      },
      "vectorize": {
        "batch_size": 10,
        "distance": "cosine",
        "kind": "openai_vectorize",
        "modality": "text",
        "provider": "pharia",
        "vector_type": "dense"
      },
      "vision_reader": {
        "batch_size": 1,
        "extra_body": {
          "chat_template_kwargs": {
            "thinking": false
          }
        },
        "max_in_flight": 16,
        "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr",
        "provider": "d_inference",
        "temperature": 0,
        "timeout": 120
      },
      "xlsx_reader": {
        "batch_size": 100,
        "kind": "excel",
        "split_level": 2
      }
    }
  }'
```

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

store.workflows("<workflow-id>").update(
    parameters=json.loads(Path("parameters.json").read_text()),
)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock workflows update <store-id> <workflow-id> \
  --parameters @parameters.json
```

Updates replace the entire `parameters` object and do not merge it. Send one of the full documents above with your change applied. If you send only the changed group, every other group reverts to its default. To switch a text workflow to the vision configuration, change `pdf_reader.kind` to `pdf_rasterizer`, add the `vision_reader` group, and send the whole document.

The change applies only to future runs. The platform does not reprocess content that is already indexed.

## Advanced: custom workflows and modules

In addition to the built-in presets, the workflow engine supports custom workflows and processing modules written in code, for example an enrichment module for a specific document type. This extension mechanism is intended for platform engineering teams, not for application developers who use the API. See [For workflow authors](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/workflow-authors.html).
